requirement:
Habeas MUST parse Rust, Python, TypeScript, CSS, Markdown, TOML, and YAML
sources with pinned tree-sitter grammars, selected by file extension compared
case-insensitively. A source with any syntax error MUST fail to parse, reporting
the line of its first error. Every
other text file MUST use a plain-text profile in which each line that is not
blank is an anonymous outline node of kind `line`. Each supported language MUST
have an outline profile that maps grammar node kinds to short outline kind names
and, for each mapped kind, states whether a node is named, and by which fields
or children, or anonymous. Only mapped kinds MUST appear in the outline, except
that a Markdown profile MAY additionally recognize colon-fenced directive
containers under {cite}`requirements.sdk.sources.markdown.fence_precedence`
and expose them as outline nodes under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.sources.markdown.fenced_blocks`. Such containers MUST
preserve source ranges and containment, and MUST NOT be recognized within
literal code or raw HTML. Other nodes MUST be transparent, so their outline
descendants appear under the nearest outline ancestor. A profile MAY attach grammar siblings to an outline
node, such as Rust attributes and doc comments preceding an item, so the outline
tree need not match the grammar tree exactly; attached siblings are part of that
node for its line range and hash. Every file's outline MUST have a root node
for the whole file, independent of language. Source in no other outline node,
such as top-level statements no profile maps, MUST belong to the root node;
profiles MUST NOT invent fallback kinds for it. Comments MUST NOT be outline nodes. Profiles MUST be
documented. Upgrading a grammar or profile MAY change outlines and MUST be
treated as a deliberate change.
rationale:
The reviewed tests cover every obligation of `requirements.references.outlines` that applies to the current profiles. I found no gap.

Mapping of obligations to tests (all in `crates/habeas-sdk/src/outline/tests.rs` unless noted):
- **Seven languages selected by extension, case-insensitively:** `profiles_are_selected_by_extension_case_insensitively` checks upper- and mixed-case extensions for Rust, Python, TSX, Markdown and TOML. It also checks that extensionless and double-extension names fall to plain text. `python_profile_outlines_defs_classes_and_statements`, `typescript_profile_outlines_declarations`, `css_profile_names_rules_by_normalized_selectors`, `markdown_profile_nests_sections_by_heading` and `toml_and_yaml_profiles_name_keys` each parse a real source for one language and assert its outline.
- **Pinned grammars:** `grammar_dependencies_are_pinned_to_exact_versions` reads each `habeas-language-*` manifest and requires every `tree-sitter-*` dependency to be an exact-version pin. The "upgrade is a deliberate change" clause is process-level. The exact pins are what enforce it.
- **Syntax error fails and reports the line of the first error:** `reports_parse_failures_with_lines` covers Rust, Python, and a TOML source with two errors. For TOML it asserts that the earlier error's line is reported and that the message is prefixed with that line. The text does not distinguish languages here, so one shared error path needs no per-language test.
- **Plain-text profile:** `plain_text_lines_are_interchangeable_anonymous_nodes` shows that blank lines are skipped and each non-blank line is an anonymous `line@…` node. The same test checks hashing by words. `outline_lists_nested_nodes_without_text_or_inputs` in `src/authoring/tools.rs` checks the `line` kind and null names for a `.txt` file.
- **Profile maps kinds, with named or anonymous nodes:** the per-language tests above assert named selectors, such as `fn[f]`, `pair[a]` and `section[Head%20*one*]`, and anonymous ones, such as `section@`, `item@` and `use@`/`macro@`. `rust_selectors_follow_syntactic_ancestry` and `selectors_name_syntactic_ancestry_and_duplicates` cover the Rust cases.
- **Only mapped kinds appear, other nodes are transparent:** `profile_rules_map_only_matching_contexts_and_keep_other_nodes_transparent` builds a profile that leaves one function unmapped. It asserts that the unmapped function is absent, that its mapped descendant is reparented to the root, and that resolving `fn[skipped]` fails. `item_macros_are_anonymous_nodes_and_expression_macros_are_not` shows that expression macros inside a function body produce no nodes.
- **Attached siblings, line range and hash:** `hashes_skip_whitespace_and_plain_comments_but_not_doc_comments` asserts that the line range starts at the doc comment and attribute, and that the hash changes when they change. `identity_hashes_include_own_attached_siblings_but_not_descendants` covers the identity side.
- **Root node for the whole file, unmapped code belongs to the root, no fallback kinds:** `resolve("")` returns the root. `file_level_inner_doc_comments_and_unmapped_code_belong_to_the_root` and the Python test check `owner_at_line` for unmapped top-level statements. `no_profile_invents_fallback_kinds` scans all profiles for `stmt`, `block`, `node` or `item` kinds and asserts that unmapped-only sources yield a root-only outline.
- **Comments are not outline nodes:** the summaries and selector lists in the Python, CSS, Markdown, TOML and YAML tests contain no comment nodes despite comments in the sources. `markdown_profile_nests_sections_by_heading` additionally asserts that the comment is recorded separately.
- **Profiles documented:** `every_profile_mapping_is_documented` checks each profile's extensions, each rule's kind and grammar kind, and the plain-text row against `md/reference.md`.
- **Redaction does not change an outline:** `redaction_never_changes_an_outline` in `crates/habeas-sdk/src/redaction/tests.rs` checks this for several languages.

**Markdown colon-fence containers:** the requirement only says a Markdown profile MAY recognize colon-fenced containers. The MUSTs on source ranges, containment, and literal code or raw HTML apply only if it does. A search of `crates/habeas-sdk/src/outline` found no colon-fence or `block` outline kind in the Markdown profile. `md/requirements/sdk/sources/markdown.md` still lists fence behavior "to settle before implementation". Nothing is implemented, so there is nothing to test here. The cited `fence_precedence` and `fenced_blocks` requirements are context only.

Every applicable MUST has a test that exercises it and asserts the outcome, and there are no acknowledged gaps.

documented. Upgrading a grammar or profile MAY change outlines and MUST be

:::{req} fence_precedence
Markdown outline parsing MUST recognize colon directive fences of three or
more colons and support nested directives with shorter inner fences. A
colon-only closing fence MUST have at least as many colons as the opener it
closes. Ordinary backtick and tilde code fences MUST follow CommonMark fence
rules and shield their contents from colon-directive recognition. Fence-like
text in inline code or raw HTML MUST NOT introduce outline directive blocks.
:::{req} fenced_blocks
The Markdown outline MUST expose colon-fenced directive containers and fenced
code blocks as anonymous `block` nodes using the shared anonymous-selector
rules under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`. A block MUST
include its opening fence, body, and closing fence when present, and MUST be
nested under its nearest enclosing outline container.
